title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Alex Chen
description:
Motivation: bring Redwood's OpenAI-compat /v1/chat.completions surface to feature parity for commonly-used parameters and semantics (roles array, stop sequences, logprobs/top_logprobs, streaming deltas and full responses, and function/tool calling framing). This change makes it practical for customers to lift-and-shift workloads from OpenAI with minimal prompt/param changes and preserves our production guarantees (latency and stability).

Summary of changes: map OpenAI chat.params to Redwood runtime equivalents (temperature, top_p, n, max_tokens -> max_output_tokens), add explicit support for 'roles' in messages and ensure role-preserving KV-caching and batching; implement stop sequence handling with derived tokenization-aware stop checks; add support for logprobs/top_logprobs in non-streaming and streaming responses (top_logprobs returned per-token when requested); unify streaming protocol so clients receive both delta messages and final 'message' with choices[].message; implement function_call passthrough and structured output hinting to support tool/function calling semantics.

Backward compatibility: defaults unchanged. When 'stream' is requested we still maintain streaming SLOs; some edge-case payloads that relied on our older streaming deltas are normalized via a compatibility shim for 3 months. Documented in docs/openai_compat.md.

Testing & rollout: extensive unit tests for parameter mapping, integration tests against the compatibility harness, added e2e tests that replay recorded OpenAI request/response pairs. Gradual rollout: feature gated behind an internal flag and enabled for canary accounts before full rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Add param mapping and validation
- [x] Implement role-aware KV cache safeguards
- [x] Implement stop/tokenization-aware stops
- [x] Streaming protocol stable: heartbeats and reassembly fixes
- [x] logprobs/top_logprobs support (stream + non-stream)
- [x] Function calling framing & passthrough
- [x] Unit + integration + e2e tests
- [x] Docs and migration notes

Notes: see detailed diffs below and the compatibility spec in docs/openai_compat.md for example request/response pairs and deprecation plan.
commits: feat(openai-compat): add mapping for chat.completions params and validation
fix(runtime/streaming): stabilize streaming delta assembly and add heartbeat handling
feat(runtime): add role-aware KV cache keying and ttl safeguards
feat(api): expose logprobs/top_logprobs path and transform to Redwood internal scoring
feat(api): function_call passthrough and structured output hints
test: add compatibility replay tests and new e2e chat_completions suite
docs: update openai_compat.md with parity notes and migration guide
small_diffs: redwood/api/openai_compat.py: added map_openai_chat_params(...) that normalizes incoming OpenAI params into RedwoodConfig objects; validates 'roles' is an array of {role, content} and rejects malformed roles

redwood/runtime/streaming.py: stabilized chunk reassembly by buffering partial token deltas and emitting heartbeat bytes every 250ms when idle; fixed race on stream close to ensure final message event is emitted
redwood/runtime/kv_cache.py: keying now includes normalized 'roles' sequence hash to avoid cache collisions when role order changes
redwood/runtime/logprobs.py: added top_k scoring path and streaming emission of per-token top_logprobs; disabled by default unless logprobs param present
review_comments: Priya Patel: Can you add more unit tests for stop sequences that include multi-byte unicode characters? Also please document how tokenization differences with OpenAI are handled.
Alex Chen: Added tests and a paragraph in docs/openai_compat.md explaining tokenization-aware stop matching and fallback to substring matching if tokenization lookup fails.
Diego Martinez: The streaming changes look good, but I worry about extra latency introduced by heartbeat ticks. Can we keep heartbeat out of hot paths?
Alex Chen: Heartbeats are emitted from a sidecar async task and don't block token assembly; added benchmarks showing <0.5ms median overhead per request in our canary cluster.
Sarah Liu: We should call out that 'top_logprobs' returns a list of maps keyed by token string; ensure the ordering and encoding are stable across languages.
Alex Chen: Confirmed and added serialization tests for top_logprobs ordering and escaping in the new test suite.
merge_commit_message: squash: openai chat.completions parity (roles, stop, logprobs, streaming, function_call)
release_notes: API: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity improvements: roles array support, stop sequence tokenization-aware handling, logprobs/top_logprobs (stream & non-stream), and function_call passthrough.
Runtime: improved streaming stability and delta reassembly; heartbeat to prevent long idle streams.
Docs: migration guide and examples added to docs/openai_compat.md.
migration_notes: Default behavior unchanged. Customers using undocumented streaming delta semantics should test against the compatibility flag. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration steps and a 3-month shim timeline.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag for canary in production in us-west-2; monitor new compat_migration_events telemetry and response_formatting_metrics. Rollback: disable flag and revert mapping to previous openai_compat path.
local_testing_instructions: python -m pytest redwood/tests/test_chat_completions.py::TestChatCompletionsParity and run redwood/examples/openai_migration against a local redis instance for KV cache validation
changelog_entry: Added OpenAI chat.completions compatibility: roles, stop sequences, logprobs, streaming parity, and function_call support. See docs/openai_compat.md for details.
